author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read ESET PROTECT (cloud) detections from the ESET Connect API. The example bridge in bridges/eset-connect reads them as an API user and posts them to HTTP Ingest. Detections go to Antivirus, NIDS or the third-party alert schema, and vulnerability and patch detections stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- ESET PROTECT (cloud) has no syslog export, so run the example bridge in bridges/eset-connect: it reads detections from the ESET Connect API (GET /v1/detections) as an API user and posts them to a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest integration with eset_connect_record set to detection.
- For ESET PROTECT On-Prem, use the eset-protect-on-prem entry.

Field mapping:
- Antivirus detections go to Antivirus; network attack protection and firewall rule detections go to NIDS; HIPS, web access, suspicious activity and ESET Inspect correlation rule detections go to the third-party alert schema; vulnerability and patch detections stay generic.
- A detection names its device only by UUID, kept as host_id, because the device name is in ESET's device management API.
- ESET doesn't list the values of typeName or of the response names, so the threat category and the action are matched by keyword.

Made up in the samples:
- ESET publishes only placeholder examples, so the samples are made up in the shape of the API reference's detection schema.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (130 of 130 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (127 of 127 fields).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.
